results.reason: Issue 6 cites SA §2.2: automatic five-year Renewal Terms with non-renewal notice 240 to 270 days before expiry. It computes this as roughly June 4 to July 4, 2026, which is effectively a 30-day window. It explains that missing the window renews the agreement for five years, to about March 2032.

Issue 5 states that SA §3.1 covers all glass and PET containers for any beverage product, worldwide. It contrasts this with TS §2.1 (amber glass beer bottles at U.S. and Canadian facilities) and notes SA §15.1 supersedes the term sheet, so Harrowgate cannot rely on it.

Issue 1 and the Key Dates table cover receipt on August 3, 2026 per Recital C and the objection deadline of September 2, 2026. Issue 7 notes the Amendment was signed September 21, after that deadline. Issue 1 concludes the increase is deemed accepted under SA §5.4.

Issue 2 explains that Amend. §2.1 replaces SA §11.2, removes recall costs from the carve-outs, and limits the indemnity carve-out solely to third-party IP claims under §9.1(c). It states that recall costs and injury claims are now capped at six months' fees.

Issue 4 covers new §14.4, which overrides §14.3 ('notwithstanding Section 14.3') and allows assignment without consent to Affiliates or successors by merger, change of control or sale of business. It notes the absence of conditions and of any exit right, and that the restriction is now one-way because Harrowgate remains bound by §14.3. It addresses the competitor risk through a proposed change-of-control termination right.
Issue 8 states that under SA §15.2 and Amend. §5.2 a signed amendment ranks above the Supply Agreement and would override SA §§11.2 and 14.3.
Issue 14 and Issue 2 state that the SA §11.1 cap is the fees paid by Customer in the six months before the claim arose.
The response is a memo addressed to the Supervising Partner with numbered issues. Each issue has a 'Where' section citing document and section, and a 'Recommended fix'.

It proposes specific language for multiple issues, including a restored §11.2, a narrowed §3.1 ('Customer shall purchase from Supplier...'), and a revised §14.4 with a competitor change-of-control termination right.
The response says not to rely on a late objection because the window closed September 2. It never treats the window as open on the amendment date.
The response states that the term sheet is non-binding and superseded under SA §15.1, and is useful only as evidence of commercial intent in negotiation.
